meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. I'm writing that down, Hale. Now, what do you have on the essay itself?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A line that isn't in the play. Show me the page, Hale, and whatever you checked it against.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence. "It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down word for word, and it goes to the principal with everything else.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn and an apology for how Owen found out. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a visit to the principal.
What moved her: owning in one sentence that you should have called before entering the zero gave you a small amount of ground, because you said it plainly and moved on.
What cost ground: bringing up Claire and saying it runs in the family cost the most, because it turned a procedure complaint into a personal one and gave her a reason to go to the principal.
Try next time: when you name the line that isn't in the play, have the page and the source you checked it against ready to show her, and leave her family out of it entirely.
